items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential opinion affirming the District of Delaware's dismissal of Thomas Yeransian's breach-of-contract complaint, which sought attorney's fees and costs under Section 8.6(b) of a Contingent Value Rights Agreement between Markel and Aspen Holdings shareholders. items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential per curiam opinion affirming the Middle District of Pennsylvania's dismissal of Libby Profitt's amended complaint against the City of Harrisburg, Capital Region Water, and the Municipal Water Authority. The complaint asserted RICO, 42 U.S.C. § 1983, Fourteenth Amendment due process, and unjust enrichment claims relating to water billing, fines, and a requirement to permit third-party access to her residence. items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential opinion affirming Jason Mattis's conviction for possession of an unregistered destructive device under 26 U.S.C. § 5861(d), arising from a flaming bottle of gasoline thrown at a Philadelphia residence. items.summary: In No. 24-1442, the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit issued an unpublished order and judgment in Jones v. Brown, et al., on interlocutory appeal from the District of Colorado. Colorado prison inmate Bernard Jones alleges that law library closure by legal assistant Yvette Brown caused him to miss a Supreme Court certiorari deadline, and that prison official Kristi Moore transferred him to another facility after he filed grievances. items.summary: A proclamation dated November 5, 2026, declares the Oval Office (Room 110), the Outer Oval Office (Rooms 106 and 108), and the Cabinet Room (Room 105) to be the Oval Office National Monument under section 320301 of title 54, United States Code. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, through the National Park Service, to manage the monument, develop a management plan in consultation with the White House Office of Administration, and require documentation and review of alternatives before any action that would substantially alter or demolish its essential architectural elements. The proclamation states that it does not restrict presidential authority to redecorate, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's structure or architectural character.

items.summary: In a Sixth Circuit opinion marked not recommended for publication, the court reviewed the 95-month prison term and 10-year supervised release imposed on Dovid Akiva Shenkman after he pled guilty to transportation and possession of child pornography. Shenkman challenged the sentence as procedurally and substantively unreasonable, including on the ground that the district court did not address his mitigation arguments concerning childhood experiences and trauma-related conditions. The court concluded that the district court adequately considered those arguments and found no error, much less plain error, on that claim.
items.title: USA v. Dovid Shenkman

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit affirmed the Eastern District of Michigan's rulings in Lorenzo Williams's suit against Ford Motor Company and a union. The panel held that Williams's 42 U.S.C. § 1981 claims against Ford were filed after the four-year limitations period under 28 U.S.C. § 1658 had expired, and that his Labor Management Relations Act § 301 fair-representation claim against the union was untimely under the six-month limitations period. The court also held that Williams's January 2022 NLRB charge did not toll the limitations period, and treated his other challenges as forfeited because his opening brief did not argue them.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the Western District of Texas's dismissal, for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, of Koshy Mathews Mathai's Federal Tort Claims Act claim for intentional infliction of emotional distress. The claim arose from a federal employer's failure to respond to Mathai's email confirming a job offer's recruitment incentive terms. The court held that the claim arose out of a misrepresentation within the exception in 28 U.S.C. § 2680(h), because the failure to respond was necessary only if the employer's earlier statements were inaccurate, and that sovereign immunity therefore barred the claim.

items.summary: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed, in a non-precedential per curiam decision, a summary judgment entered for Safeco Insurance Company of Indiana in Torry Hull v. Safeco Insurance Company of Indiana, which concerned a claim for water damage from an attic condenser-line leak. The court upheld the district court's exclusion of an expert affidavit disclosed after discovery closed and held that the estimate and the plaintiff's testimony did not show that the additional repairs were caused by a covered loss, so the breach-of-contract and bad-faith claims failed. The court also concluded that Safeco had good cause for refusing the additional payment because its adjuster had conducted an onsite inspection of the home.
items.title: Torry Hull v. Safeco Insurance Company of Indiana

Collins, decided November 4, 2026, affirming a decision of the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims. items.summary: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed a 46-month sentence imposed on Derick Desir, who pleaded guilty to conspiracy and to making false statements in firearms dealer records under 18 U.S.C. §§ 371 and 924(a)(1)(A). Desir challenged a four-level firearms-trafficking enhancement under U.S.S.G. § 2K2.1(b)(5) and a four-level enhancement under § 2K2.1(b)(6)(A) for firearms transported out of the United States. The court held that the district court did not err in applying the trafficking enhancement based on the circumstances known to Desir, and it reviewed the second enhancement under plain-error review.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. (Tecnam) Model P2006T airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of damage on the engine mount structure caused by defective non-conforming engine shock mounts being installed. This proposed AD would require inspecting for the installation of non-conforming engine shock mounts and replacing any non-conforming engine shock mount with an approved part. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of a non-conforming engine shock mount on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 721 [EPA-HQ-OPPT-2025-2169; FRL-13126-03-OCSPP] RIN 2070-AB27 Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25-3.5e) AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). ACTION: Final rule.
items.summary: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.
items.title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25-3.5e)

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 62 [EPA-R03-OAR-2026-5021; FRL-13501-01-R3] Approval and Promulgation of Delegation of Authority for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Allegheny County; Delegation of Authority of the Federal
items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a request from the Allegheny County Health Department (ACHD) for delegation of authority to implement and enforce the Federal Plan requirements for existing Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) landfills within Allegheny County in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. On May 21, 2021, the EPA promulgated the Federal Plan for MSW landfills to fulfill the requirements of section 111(d) of the Clean Air Act (CAA). The Federal Plan addresses the implementation and enforcement of the emission guidelines applicable to existing MSW landfills located in areas not covered by an approved and currently effective State plan. The Federal Plan imposes emission limits and other control requirements for existing MSW landfills which will reduce designated pollutants.
items.title: Approval and Promulgation of Delegation of Authority for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Allegheny County; Delegation of Authority of the Federal Plan for Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 62 [EPA-R03-OAR-2023-0230; FRL-9329-03-R3] Approval and Promulgation of State Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; West Virginia; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Wast
items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is approving a Clean Air Act (CAA) section 111(d) plan revision submitted by the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection (WVDEP). This revision updates the plan to include changes made to Emissions Guidelines and Compliance Times for municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills. This action is being taken under the Clean Air Act (CAA).
items.title: Approval and Promulgation of State Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; West Virginia; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 62 [EPA-R09-OAR-2026-5710; FRL-13516-01-R9] Approval and Promulgation of State Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Arizona; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Lan
items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State plan submitted by the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD). This plan pertains to the regulation of landfill gas and its components from existing municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13800; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01663-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administrati
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319-111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes

items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or “Act”) requirements for the 2015 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or “standards”) in the San Joaquin Valley ozone nonattainment area (“San Joaquin Valley” or “SJV”). In this document, the EPA refers to these submissions collectively as the “SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP.” The EPA proposes to approve the SJV 70 parts per billion (ppb) Ozone SIP as meeting the applicable ozone nonattainment area requirements for emissions inventories, reasonably available control measures, attainment demonstration, rate of progress and reasonable further progress, motor vehicle emissions budgets, and enhanced monitoring. The EPA is also initiating the adequacy process for the budgets included in this SIP submission through this proposed rule. The EPA also proposes to approve two SIP revisions amending the SIP to incorporate changes reflecting updates to California Air Resources Board (CARB) Consumer Products Regulations and Method 310, which apply statewide and upon which the SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP relies. items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or “Department”) portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or “Act”) requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.
items.title: Air Plan Revisions; Arizona; Maricopa County Air Quality Department; New Source Review; Emission Reduction Credits

items.opening_verbatim: LEGAL SERVICES CORPORATION 45 CFR Parts 1630 and 1631 Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management AGENCY: Legal Services Corporation. ACTION: Final rule. SUMMARY: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation'
items.summary: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC or Corporation) regulations governing cost allowability, prior approval requirements, and property and procurement standards applicable to LSC recipients. The final rule clarifies when recipients must obtain prior approval for expenditures of LSC funds; increases the monetary threshold for prior approval; clarifies the treatment of proceeds from fundraising activities supported with LSC funds; provides additional flexibility in LSC's review of prior approval requests; clarifies documentation requirements for prior approval requests; and revises the deadline and requirements for accounting for LSC funds invested in real estate. These amendments are intended to clarify existing requirements, reduce administrative burden, promote consistent oversight and enforcement, and strengthen accountability in the use of Federal funds.
items.title: Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management

items.opening_verbatim: LEGAL SERVICES CORPORATION 45 CFR Part 1631 Purchasing and Property Management AGENCY: Legal Services Corporation. ACTION: Notice of proposed rulemaking. SUMMARY: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition
items.summary: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of “capital improvement” by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property.
items.title: Purchasing and Property Management

items.opening_verbatim: Title 3— The President Notice of November 3, 2026 Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Iran On November 14, 1979, by Executive Order 12170, the President declared a national emergency with respect to Iran pursuant to the I
items.summary: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency with respect to Iran that was declared in Executive Order 12170 on November 14, 1979, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. The notice states that relations with Iran have not yet normalized and that the process of implementing the agreements with Iran dated January 19, 1981 is ongoing. It also states that this emergency is distinct from the emergency declared in Executive Order 12957 on March 15, 1995, and from the emergency renewal of March 2, 2026.
items.title: Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Iran

items.summary: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12938 on November 14, 1994, concerning the proliferation of nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons and the means of delivering them. The notice states that Executive Order 12938 was amended by Executive Order 13094 on July 28, 1998 and by Executive Order 13382 on June 28, 2005. It states that the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction continues to pose a threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States.
items.title: Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction

items.opening_verbatim: Notice of November 3, 2026 Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Situation in Nicaragua On November 27, 2018, by Executive Order 13851, the President declared a national emergency pursuant to the International Emergency
items.summary: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13851 on November 27, 2018, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, with respect to the situation in Nicaragua. The notice references Executive Order 14088 of October 24, 2022, which took additional steps with respect to that emergency. It states that the situation in Nicaragua, including the government's response to protests that began on April 18, 2018 and its treatment of democratic institutions and the rule of law, continues to pose a threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States.
items.title: Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Situation in Nicaragua

items.opening_verbatim: Notice of November 3, 2026 Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Companies of the People's Republic of China On November 12, 2020, by Executive Order 13959, the Pr
items.summary: A notice dated November 3, 2026 continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959 on November 12, 2020, as expanded in scope by Executive Order 14032 on June 3, 2021, concerning the threat from securities investments that finance certain companies of the People's Republic of China. The notice states that the PRC's Military-Civil Fusion strategy and certain uses and development of Chinese surveillance technology continue to pose a threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States. It states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond November 12, 2026, pursuant to section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act.
items.title: Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Companies of the People's Republic of China
